component.name: Canalis
component.summary: Route and process audio on the PipeWire desktop

description.p: Canalis is a console for the Linux desktop's audio: virtual microphones and outputs, a target for every app, DAW-style effect chains with built-in Claritas DSP and CLAP plugins, and a patchbay. A chain is itself a device, so apps see "Desktop EQ" as an output and "Voice for calls" as a microphone. Everything is remembered by name and comes back at login.
Works with WirePlumber's defaults and targets instead of around them.

screenshot.caption: Chains: effect strips that apps see as outputs and microphones
Devices: outputs, inputs and virtual devices with their defaults
Apps: every app that plays or records, and where it goes
Graph: the patchbay of every node and link

description.p: Packaging only, no change to the app itself. The Flatpak shows the tray icon, so the service can be quit from there. On Fedora the install command adds the COPR and on Debian and Ubuntu the signed APT repository, so system updates keep Canalis current.

The first public release. One command installs Canalis on any distribution: the .rpm on Fedora, the .deb on Ubuntu and Debian, or a new tarball under your home folder elsewhere, each checked against SHA256SUMS. canalis --version prints the version. The logo intro plays on every launch except from the tray. Inside the Flatpak, plugins come from Flathub's LinuxAudio extensions, LV2 works, and Run at login uses the Background portal.

A/B compare, automatic level, a live spectrum, safe start after crashes and undo for chain edits. A soundboard with its own Pads tab, MIDI learn for any plugin parameter, keybind commands, device rules and desktop notifications. Graph selection, groups and a minimap. Italian, French and German. A chain no longer crashes when its outputs change.
First release: devices, apps, chains with Claritas EQ and CLAP plugins, graph, autostart.
